entries.title: Searing Gorge
body: A gorge of black rock and rivers of lava north of Blackrock Mountain, torn open when the Dark Iron sorcerer-thane Thaurissan summoned Ragnaros. Fire elementals, lava spiders and golems roam it, and the air is so hot that dwarves joke their fingers swell up like sausages.

The Dark Iron dwarves work it as a vast mine and forge. At its centre lies the Cauldron, a pit where enslaved workers dig and smelt around the clock, watched by four sentry towers. A gate guarded by a stubborn dwarven mountaineer keeps it closed to the Badlands, and a few hardy outsiders camp along its edges.
sources: page text 1914 (War of the Three Hammers)
pre-Cataclysm lore: the summoning of Ragnaros

entries.title: The Cauldron
body: A vast open pit in the middle of the Searing Gorge where the Dark Irons mine and smelt thorium. Taskmasters and slavers drive the slave workers, heavy war golems patrol the ramps, and the Slag Pit beneath it holds the workers' sleeping quarters and pools of lava full of incendosaurs.
Four sentry towers stand on the rim, the Cauldron's first line of defence. Dwarves work here whose minds are no longer their own, bound by the power of the Suntara stones.

entries.title: Thorium Point
body: A camp on the north-western ridge above the gorge, home of the Thorium Brotherhood. Its smiths are Dark Iron dwarves who broke with their kin and the Firelord, and keep their own secret recipes, including fiery flux.

They are not friends of the Dark Irons in the Cauldron. They pay bounties on stolen tools, on taskmasters and slavers, and on Overseer Maltorius, a rogue Brotherhood agent who sold the flux recipe to the Cauldron's masters for a promotion. Both factions' flight masters stay close by, and keep a wary eye on the Dark Iron neighbours.

entries.title: Firewatch Ridge
body: A ridge in the north-west of the gorge where the Twilight's Hammer have made a large encampment. Their idolaters carry symbols of Ragnaros and pray to him, and welcome intruders as fresh blood for sacrifice.

In a cage among them sits a night elf, Zamael Lunthistle. He has done countless malevolent things against the world and expects no absolution, but his faith has returned, and he asks that his prayer to Elune, etched on a golden tablet the cultists took, be carried to Darnassus.

entries.title: Grimesilt Dig Site
body: A Dark Iron dig in the gorge where their geologists work with magic.

Someone ran from them, hid in the outhouse to get out of sight, and was locked in. His name is Locheed. He would like help, some silk cloth for... nothing, and eventually the key, which the Dark Irons hid.

entries.title: Stonewrought Pass
body: The pass that links the Searing Gorge to the Badlands and Loch Modan, closed by a great gate. Mountaineer Pebblebitty guards it on the far side and will not let anyone in, because if he lets one in he must let everybody in.
He has one weakness: Margol the Rager, a giant beast whose horn still carries the head of his broken axe. Bring him the real thing, proven by Ironforge's curator, and he will hand over the key.

entries.title: Kalaran Windblade
body: A grim warrior who camps in the Searing Gorge and swears vengeance on the Dark Irons. He tells a sad story to anyone who will listen, and asks them to help him set the Cauldron's four sentry towers ablaze.

He forges a Torch of Retribution from hearts of flame, golem oil, Dark Iron thorium and a symbol of Ragnaros, and his squire hails the burning towers as glorious. Those who help him find their deeds known to the black dragonflight. Kalaran's true name is Kalaran the Deceiver.
sources: quest 4022 description (the flight is aware of your work in the Searing Gorge)

entries.title: Obsidion and the Suntara Stones
body: An Explorers' League team led by Dorius Stonetender came to the gorge seeking the Suntara stones. Dorius was shot fleeing to Ironforge; his last letter told his brother, Curator Thorius, that the Dark Iron Lathoric the Black was using the stones to enslave the team, their minds twisted to build something called Obsidion.

The dying archaeologists asked to be released. It had all been a trap. Thorius' own brother had arranged it, and betrayed Ironforge. Thorius took it as proof that the influence of the Old Gods is still strong in these lands.
